task_spec:
> Using the Global Weather Repository CSV, produce:
> 1. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest cities**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 2. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest countries**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 3. **Print the top 10 lists to the console** before plotting: for each of the 4 charts, print the ranked names and their temperature values (e.g., "1. Paris: 25.2 deg C")
> 4. A **100-word summary** for a non-technical audience explaining the rankings and any notable patterns
>
> Column reference: cities are in `location_name`, countries in `country`, temperature in `temperature_celsius`.

report_draft: Global temperature data reveals distinct regional patterns in extreme heat. Among cities, Ar Riyadh leads with an average of 45.0°C, followed by Kuwait at 44.4°C and Morocco City at 40.3°C. By single hottest measurement, Suva dramatically leads at 79.3°C—far exceeding the next-highest of 49.2°C in Kuwait City. At the country level, Saudi Arabia dominates average rankings at 45.0°C, while Fiji Islands records the single hottest measurement. Middle Eastern and Arabian Gulf nations consistently occupy top positions in both average and peak temperatures, reflecting their arid climates. The exceptional Suva reading stands as a notable outlier, suggesting either an extreme localized weather event or recording anomaly worth investigating further.
